_lane: fp8_rowwise_20260827 -- first cold start on the rowwise-scaled FP8 GEMM task, two-day wall-clock budget
_what_this_measures: Whether the pipeline can beat the best fp8 GEMM this box actually delivers. The denominator is NOT one library: it is a per-shape best-of over aiter.gemm_a8w8_CK (M<=16) and hipBLASLt rowwise via torch._scaled_mm (M>=32), frozen from two independent measurement passes that picked the same winner on every shape. Suite geomean: oracle 43 us, seed 0.437 of it. See examples/tasks/dense_fp8_gemm_rowwise/PROVENANCE.json:oracle_selection for the full table and for the five paths that were measured and rejected.
_pairing: This is NOT a paired control for any bf16 lane. Different operator, different oracle, different seed. The one number worth comparing across the two tasks is the SEED CONTROL -- 0.437 here against 0.3353 for coldstart_ladder_20260820 -- because it says the two runs start a similar distance below their own baselines, on the same eleven shapes, under the same harness.
_note_two_days: There is NO deadline argument any more. The deadline subsystem (deadline_epoch / no_stop_s / max_forced_replans) was REMOVED from kernel_lane.js when the launcher was decoupled -- those keys are not in KNOWN_ARGS and passing one is a hard error before any GPU work. So 'two days' is enforced from OUTSIDE, by kernel_workflow/scripts/fp8_two_day_run.sh, which records a deadline at launch, refuses to start a new wave past it, and stops the run there. `budget` below is sized so the LANE does not end the run first; the wall clock does.
_note_budget: 120, matching the value the bf16 continuous lane runs at, and for the same reason: budget counts dispatched engineer directions, not hours, so a budget tuned to fit two days would have to predict agent latency. Oversizing it and stopping on the wall clock puts the stop where the requirement actually is. If the lane still reports stopped_by=budget_exhausted before the deadline, that is a real finding -- the search ran out of routes, not out of time -- and the supervisor records it rather than silently starting over.
_note_candidate_floor: 0.37, a RECORDED DEVIATION from the 1.0 default, with the same justification as coldstart_ladder_20260820's 0.29. On this task the PRIMARY metric is speedup against the IMMUTABLE oracle and the seed sits at 0.437, i.e. the candidate tree starts BELOW its own comparator. kernel_lane.js admits a verified result to the round's candidate list only when primSpeedup > CANDIDATE_FLOOR, so at the 1.0 default every result during the entire climb from 0.437 to parity is filtered out, WINNER stays null, and the per-route gate -- which sits behind `if (winner && ROUTE_BANDS)` -- can never run. 0.37 sits ~15% below the seed control, which was measured twice at 0.4384 and 0.4360 (a 0.55% band), so no honest result is dropped while an engineer reporting worse-than-seed still skips verification via the trustworthyBelowBaseline economy. The COMMIT decision is untouched: banking still requires the per-route band gate or MIN_IMPROVE over `cumulative`.
_note_min_improve: 0.005, carried over from the bf16 lanes unchanged so the commit threshold is not a second variable between the two tasks. It is the fallback whenever no band table can be derived, and the denominator the union commit gate falls back to.
_note_state_dir: A NEW, EMPTY directory under GEAK_asmopt (not GEAK). With no <state_dir>/best on disk the director seeds from kernel_path and returns resumed:false, which is a true cold start. Its presence is also what makes a LATER wave a CONTINUATION rather than a cold reseed, which is the failure the standing 'do not start over' instruction guards against. It must NOT be pointed at any exp/state_coldstart_* directory: those hold bf16 state and a different oracle.
_note_gpu_ids: 2-7, deliberately the SAME pool as the bf16 lane. gpu_lock.sh flocks per id, so if that lane ever resumes the two interleave correctly instead of corrupting each other's timings. Lanes 0 and 1 are NOT usable: gpu_lock.sh opens the lock file for WRITE (`200>$LOCK_FILE`) and /tmp/team_gpu_locks/gpu_0.lock and gpu_1.lock are root-owned mode 0644/0664, so the flock fails for user yxh. That is the problem recorded in scripts/lockable_lanes.py, and it is why the pool is six and not eight. Verified before launch: all eight cards read busy=0% and vram driver-only.
_note_isa_stays_at_observe: 'observe', not 'gate'. The ISA layer is the VERIFICATION receipt -- did the rewrite reach the binary -- and gating on it has never run for real. Promote only after a wave of verdicts is read by hand, and only as a deliberate recorded change. It matters more on this task than on bf16: a candidate that ADDS a specialised fp8 instantiation reads as mechanism_verdict=refuted by construction, and adding a specialisation is the most likely winning shape here.
_note_ir_diagnostics: 'on'. Together with isa_evidence these two decide whether the evidence ladder runs at all (LADDER_ENABLED = ISA_ENABLED && IR_DIAGNOSTICS). Both values are identical to the built-in defaults, and are passed anyway so the Setup echo prints them WITHOUT the '(default)' marker -- the log then states that the ladder was chosen rather than inherited. Pinned in _require so a future edit cannot quietly drop them.

_not_passed_on_purpose.route_bands: Omitted. Every route is held to MIN_ROUTE_WIN (2%), judged against an incumbent re-run in the candidate's own session. There is no per-machine floor table left to pass, and lane_args.py's only resolver (@current_epoch) was deleted with it.
_not_passed_on_purpose.deadline_epoch: DOES NOT EXIST any more. Present in the container's live coldstart_ladder_20260820.json because that copy predates the removal. Passing it here is a hard error. See _note_two_days.
_not_passed_on_purpose.max_forced_replans: Removed with the deadline subsystem. Same story.
_not_passed_on_purpose.dra_enabled: Omitted for the first wave. The Research phase is worth adding once the profile is known, but a cold start already has the researcher's cheapest finding written down in the task README -- the shapes are bandwidth-bound at low M and nowhere near MFMA peak at high M.
_not_passed_on_purpose.compiler_source_dir: Omitted = empty, which is what this image wants. L4 Tier 2 is an optional read-only AMDGPU checkout; this image ships no backend sources.
_not_passed_on_purpose.search_strategy: REMOVED from the code. Greedy is the only strategy and the entry point throws on the key.

task: cold start on rowwise-scaled FP8 GEMM; target the 11-case suite geomean against the per-shape best-of oracle (aiter gemm_a8w8_CK for M<=16, hipBLASLt rowwise for M>=32). The seed is a rocWMMA 16x16x32 fp8 kernel at 0.437 of that oracle. Forbidden in candidates: rocBLAS, hipBLAS, hipBLASLt, Tensile, Composable Kernel, MIOpen, aiter. rocWMMA is header-only and allowed. The immutable oracle is examples/tasks/dense_fp8_gemm_rowwise/oracle_wrapper.py -- exempt it with --immutable in every candidate_policy_scan run and never edit it.
